claim_en: TWO NAMED GRADES OF SACRED CRAFT. maase choshev ('the work of the designer') rendered ovad OMAN ('the work of the MASTER-CRAFTSMAN' — the inner curtains and the veil, cherubim woven into the fabric) against maase rokem rendered ovad TZAYYAR ('the work of the EMBROIDERER' — the outer door-screen): a rank-order of craft the translation keeps distinct, higher art for the inner house.

THE STANDING WOOD. atzei shittim OMDIM rendered KAYEMIN ('STANDING/ENDURING') — the token the chain reads doubly: boards standing as the tree grew, and boards that endure forever. The testing shelf's pointer: Mishnah Sukkah 3:14 anchors on this verse in the enumeration.

THE BUILDING HAS A HALAKHAH. ve-hakemota et ha-mishkan KE-MISHPATO ('according to its fashion') rendered u-tekim yat mashkena KE-HILKHETEI ('according to ITS HALAKHAH' — its RULE): the received translation applies the law-word itself to the assembly order — architecture under statute; closed by the shown-pattern clause (di itchazeta be-tura, 'which you were shown in the mountain').

source: Onkelos on Exod 26:33-35; the case row at Mishnah Yoma 5:1
claim_en: ONE CURTAIN, ONE BOUNDARY — AND EVERY VESSEL'S STATION. ve-tafresh parukhta lekhon ben kudsha u-ven kodesh kudshaya ('and the veil shall SEPARATE FOR YOU between the Holy and the Holy of Holies') — graded sanctity in a single clause (its Second-Temple case row: Mishnah Yoma 5:1, the two curtains and the cubit between); the floor-plan follows as standing law — the cover on the ark within, the table on the NORTH, the menorah opposite on the SOUTH (26:34-35).

THE BOARDS' PROVENANCE AND THE MIDDLE BAR'S JOURNEY. Jacob planted the cedars going down to Egypt, telling his sons the redemption would ask for a tabernacle — plant now; the cedars SANG; twenty-four species, the shittah alone chosen — and THE MIDDLE BAR of our 26:28 WENT DOWN TO EGYPT IN JACOB'S HAND: this chapter's own fixture given a Genesis provenance. The shittim-name heals Shittim (sinned there, struck there, healed by its wood — Joel 4:18's spring watering that very ravine).

source: Babylonian Talmud Sukkah 45b (via Mishnah Sukkah 3:14's enumeration anchor; Step 9 Terumah exam)
claim_en: THE STANDING-WORD BECOMES AN ORIENTATION LAW. From our 26:15's own token — acacia wood, STANDING — the Talmud derives that commandment objects are taken the way they grow, upright as they stood (Babylonian Talmud Sukkah 45b); the lulav rows are its case neighborhood. Talmud-only provenance: no Mishnah states the rule.
middah: plain (standing read as the way they grow — the orientation law; Sukkah 45b, Talmud only)

claim_en: THE STRUCTURE'S BABYLONIAN LAYER. The middle bar's STANDING MIRACLE (by miracle it stood — the architecture's honest impossibility, landing beside EX26-05's Jacob-planted provenance); the beam-taper dispute (R. Yehuda's fingerbreadth by tamim-as-ended against R. Nechemiah's cubit-throughout by yachdav, each answering the other's token, the corner geometry and curtain overhang computed both ways); the partition's one-or-two (R. Yosei's single curtain from the divide-verb; the Rabbis' two at the second Temple's doubtful cubit); the craft-words' diagnostic (needle work one face, weaving two); the cherubim's angled resolution taught in the name of ONKELOS THE CONVERT — 'like a student taking leave of his teacher' — the corpus' own translator cited by name on the build's ink; and the onyx list-boundary parse at the letter grain. Filed F-100, auto-seated (round 26, the sanctuary block).
middah: plain (the middle bar's standing miracle; the taper dispute on each other's tokens; the craft-words' diagnostic; Onkelos cited by name)
